Long-delayed, but my talk notes are up! It's the perfect nerdy #Mesh distraction for a long holiday weekend.

I presented "Mesh Networking in Collapse: #Meshtastic, #MeshCore, #Reticulum" almost 2 months ago at @bsidescle in 2026. For each one I cover basics before diving into message forwarding, encryption, and even byte-level packet formats. Get a primer on how each one works so you can pick the right tool for the job!

Some take-aways:
- Meshtastic is a good intro, great for small-ish ad-hoc situations like camping
- Meshcore good for a larger local/regional network
- Reticulum has strongest encryption and is very flexible, good long-term vision, steeper learning/usability curve

Let me know what you think!

4. My MeshCore / Meshtastic weather script is working pretty well, going to add a few more …

Charlie 🐧💻🛠️ (@cdp1337@social.bitsnbytes.dev) · 🔁 2 · ❤️ 2 · 💬 0

My MeshCore / Meshtastic weather script is working pretty well, going to add a few more features like enabling/disabling various automation features like weather alerts, current conditions, and alerts, (currently they are all just enabled).

It can also do NL-based direct message support for queries like "how hot is it" which maps to the "temperature" command, MQTT uploads for acting as an observer, onboard sensors with fallback to openweathermap, and wifi upload of sensor data to HomeAssistant.

Any weather or mesh folks have ideas for other features to add?

OH, and unlike OpenHop, it's actually configured to run on an SD card without burning through write cycles and can connect to radios configured for standard companion mode.
